To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cross sections for pion production in heavy-ion collisions are much higher than the cross sections for proton-induced collisions.

(1) the pion production cross-sections in the subthreshold region are well described by an exponential energy dependence; and (2) the exponential slope factors are in good agreement with the predictions of a statistical model, in which the pions are produced in the decay of the intermediate Δ-resonance.
the pion spectra at 90° for the 14N + C system at 41A MeV, 67A MeV, and 80A MeV have a slope factor of 1.1, 1.3, and 1.5 MeV, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of negative pions in subthreshold heavy-ion collisions.
the production of charged pions in heavy ion collisions.
the investigation of the production of pions in the reaction 14N+C at 135, 80, 67 and 41A MeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data do not exclude any of the models considered here.
the data are consistent with a mechanism where pions are emitted from a hot source with a temperature of 30-40 MeV.
the production mechanism of negative pions in subthreshold heavy-ion collisions is not yet understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the production of negative pions in subthreshold heavy-ion collisions can be understood in terms of a nucleon-nucleus reaction, where the pions are mainly produced by pion-nucleon scattering in the nuclear medium.
the pion production mechanism is dominated by a nucleon exchange process, which is strongly enhanced by a Δ resonance in the intermediate state.
the production of energetic pions is dominated by the excitation of giant resonance states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pion production in the subthreshold region is dominated by the direct process, and the pion production cross section is proportional to the number of participant nucleon pairs in the collisions.
the pion production mechanism is not understood at these low energies.
the production of energetic pions is a complex phenomenon that involves several mechanisms.
